<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Seats hold holdings and claims across compactions, but a compaction can end the seat's turn with nothing queued, and nothing wakes it. This adds one daemon-side wake per compaction, inside the existing watchdog round. One coder (tapir).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A seat holding work that a compaction leaves idle gets one resume message naming its holdings, so it never sits idle for hours.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing how or when seats are compacted.
- Waking seats with no holdings or claims.
- Any per-tick per-seat work.

| ac-0001 | A seat that holds work is woken once after a compaction leaves it idle. When a seat that holds a live role holding (any role/instance in the directory) or an open claim has been compacted (a delivered compact control, or a completed memory-turn compact) and then goes idle with nothing queued for it, the daemon sends it ONE normal message from pij-bg: 'resume: you hold &lt;holdings and claims&gt;; re-read your handover and continue, or tell your parent if you're blocked.' Once per compaction, never repeated for the same one; a seat that records its own activity before going idle, or has something queued, isn't sent it. <a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

F111 (pm-001, 08 Nov): pij-exuberant-wildcat held coder/215 for about 17 hours without working: after a compaction ended its turn, nothing woke it (it answered a status check at 06:42 with its context intact). The prime (06:49): encode it in the daemon: when a seat holding a role holding or a claim goes idle right after a compaction with nothing queued, send it one 'resume: you hold <holdings>; re-read your handover' message, once per compaction, inside the existing round, no launches; badger's sweep covers it until then. Compaction is visible to the daemon as a compact control send (pij send --command compact) and as memory-turn holds (memory_turn {action: compact}).

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
- Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
- One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
